newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Peters hints at company tax news in budget.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Peters hints at company tax news in budget.

text.p: New Zealand's Treasurer Winston Peters on Tuesday left open the possibility of an announcement on corporate tax rates in the budget due in June.
Peters was asked in parliament whether he had seen reports that current corporate tax rates were contributing to a fall in business confidence and, if so, what he planned to do.

"I think it is fair to say that with respect to that matter and others, it is an ongoing consideration of the government and its coalition partners and the member will have to wait for budget night for an announcment on those things," he replied.
United MP and former revenue minister Peter Dunne, who asked the question, said he was surprised by the answer.
"The reason I asked was that the combination of the new disputes and penalties regime and the current level of corporate rates have been cited as causing a lack of confidence.

"I anticipated an answer that at some time in the future they would review it. Peters' suggestion that maybe there might be something in the budget goes a little further than I had expected," Dunne told Reuters.
The government has postponed until 1998 this year's planned cut from 21.5 to 19.5 percent in the personal tax rate on income up to NZ$38,000.
Dunne said a fall in the corporate rate of 33 percent was sure to be tied to a parallel move in the personal rate, where the top income tax rate is currently also 33 percent.

"It has always been accepted that you can't have the top rates unaligned. Maybe he will use (the budget) to foreshadow what might occur in the future, but I am a little bit surprised he answered the question in the open way he has," Dunne added.
